title: A `require` or `autoload` literal, an `as class<T>` string and a string argument at a path or class-name parameter complete, link and hover as the path or name the compiler reads, and a directory link reveals it in the Explorer
scope:
Completion, links, hover and go-to-definition inside the literals of `require` and `autoload`, inside the string
operand of `as class<T>` and inside a string argument at a parameter marked as a path or a class name, the trigger
characters that open those lists, and what the VS Code client does with a link to a directory. Any other string is not
decided here.
dependsOnText:
[0099](0099.md) (the request set, and `documentLink` as a projection of the walk), [0193](0193.md)
(trigger characters answered only where a spelling ends), [0241](0241.md) (the path and class-name marks, and the
checker's resolved path literals).

summary.headline: Paths and class names complete and link in the editor
summary.body:
Inside the path of a `require` or an `autoload` declaration, the editor lists the folders and `.nvs` files in the
folder the path reaches, and ctrl+click on a folder shows it in the Explorer. A path you pass to a function
that reads or writes a file lists every file and folder, opens the file on ctrl+click and shows its full path on
hover. An `autoload` prefix lists the namespaces your code declares. A class
name in a string, in `'App\User' as class<Model>` or `Core\Reflect::forClass('App\User')`, lists your classes and
opens the class on ctrl+click.
